# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for OKF-11 # Review — OKF-11 ## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — private concept titles and descriptions leak onto public index pages (FR-3) ## Context - Run ID: agent-okf-11-review-2aa74173 - Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/okf/workspaces/feature-okf-11/.pan/review/agent-okf-11-review-2aa74173/context.json - Branch / workspace: feature/okf-11 / /home/eltmon/Projects/okf/workspaces/feature-okf-11 - PR: https://github.com/eltmon/okf/pull/12 - HEAD reviewed: 2aa74173bb2314309c2d855ca33c3cb21cf5a47d - Base / prior cycle SHA: origin/main 92a21febed99895716eabc648f0ba88467fd01ab (PR base); no prior review cycle. The local `main` ref in this worktree points at an unrelated history (fe73d46), so every diff here is against `origin/main`. ## Blocking Findings ### [security/requirements] Index filtering misses listing lines that `reindex.py` generates, so private titles and descriptions get published — `scripts/publish_render.py:59` - Severity: ! (MUST) - Classification / requirement scope: in_pr_scope (new `kept_index_lines`). It breaks FR-3 ("A private concept appears nowhere on the site … Its index listing line is dropped"). It also contradicts the shipped docs: references/publish.md says "What is never published: Private concepts, and their titles in index listings", and the README says "A private concept has no page, no index line". Triggers 1 and 3 are an **implementation defect**: the filter's link detection is narrower than what reindex produces and the renderer prints. Trigger 2 is a **specification defect**. PRD §4.6 says "Drop the line when that link is a concept that is not public … **Keep every other line unchanged.**" The code follows that, so a multi-line description's continuation line survives. Spec correction: inside the `OKF:INDEX` markers, drop a dropped item's continuation lines, and keep only lines that positively resolve to a public concept or a published directory. All three triggers still block, because FR-3 fails either way. - Trigger and changed-code connection: `kept_index_lines` decides whether to drop a listing line by running `okf_common.LINK_PATTERN.search(line)`. That regex is `\[[^\]]+\]\(([^)\s]+)…\)`. When it finds no match, the line is kept unchanged. Then `render_markdown` renders the line with its own bracket-depth parser (`_find_closing_bracket` / `_parse_destination`), which does recognise the link. The resolver returns `None` for the private target, so the link text and the rest of the line render as plain text. `scripts/reindex.py` (unchanged, lines 28-35) writes listing lines as `* [{title}]({file}){ - description}` using the raw title and raw description. So the standard `/okf sync` → reindex flow produces lines that hit this gap in two ways: 1. **The title contains `]`** (for example `Layoffs [draft]`, `Outage [2026-11-01]`, or an unbalanced `a] b`). LINK_PATTERN cannot match `[Layoffs [draft]](secret-plan.md)`, so the line is kept. The page shows `Layoffs [draft] - `. 2. **The description has several lines** (YAML `description: |`). reindex writes the second line of the description as its own line, which does not start with `* `. Only the first line is classified and dropped. The continuation line is kept and renders as a paragraph on the public page. 3. **The filename contains a space** (`rules/my file.md`). reindex writes `* [Space file](my file.md) - …`. LINK_PATTERN's target class `[^)\s]+` does not match it. The renderer's `_parse_destination` does not match it either, so the whole line, filename included, renders as literal text. - Expected / observed / impact: expected: the private concept is absent from `rules/index.html`. Observed: its title and description appear in the public HTML. `--check` exits 0, because no redaction rule matches. So nothing warns the author, and the private text ships on a public site. Preventing exactly this is the purpose of the feature. - Evidence: runtime reproduction against the fixture copy under the session scratchpad (probe4). I added two private concepts, `rules/secret-plan.md` (`title: Layoffs [draft]`, `description: ZZ-LEAK-DESC …`) and `rules/hr.md` (`description: |` with a second line `ZZ-LEAK-SECOND-LINE about Bob`). Then I ran the real `scripts/reindex.py --bundle b`, `publish.py --bundle b --check` and `publish.py --bundle b --out out`: ``` reindex=0 ok - publish check passed: 3 public concept(s), no redaction rule matches ok - published 3 public concept(s) to out (4 private excluded, 0 redaction(s) applied) $ grep -o "ZZ-LEAK[^<]*\|Layoffs[^<]*" out/rules/index.html ZZ-LEAK-SECOND-LINE about Bob Layoffs [draft] - ZZ-LEAK-DESC fire the night crew ``` Probe 5 (scratchpad probe5) adds `rules/my file.md` (private, `description: ZZ-LEAK-SPACE`) and `rules/unbal.md` (private, `title: "a] ZZ-LEAK-UNBAL"`). It also runs reindex, `--check` (exit 0) and `--out`: ``` [Space file](my file.md) - ZZ-LEAK-SPACE [a] ZZ-LEAK-UNBAL](unbal.md) - ZZ-LEAK-UNBAL-DESC ``` `validate.py` does not restrict titles, descriptions or filenames, so all these inputs are valid OKF. - Fix (must fail closed). Probe 5 shows that switching to the renderer's own parser is **not enough**: `_parse_destination` also fails on the space and unbalanced-bracket lines, so they would still be kept as literal text. Pick one of these: - **(a)** Inside the ``…`END` block, keep a line only when it positively resolves to a public concept or a published directory. Drop every other line in the block, continuation lines included. - **(b)** Ignore the marker block's contents and regenerate it from the model, reusing `generated_listing`. Keep the hand-written prose outside the markers. Outside the markers, the current behaviour (link text stays) is documented and acceptable. Add regression tests for a bracketed title, an unbalanced `]` title, a filename with a space and a multi-line description, all on private concepts. Each test asserts that no private title, description or filename reaches any output file. ## Non-blocking Findings ### [security] `search_text` leaves private link targets in `search-index.json` when the link text contains brackets — `scripts/publish_search.py:15` - Severity: ~ (SHOULD) - Classification: implementation defect, in_pr_scope. It has the same root cause as the blocker: a regex link matcher that disagrees with the renderer. - Trigger: a public body contains `[notes [v2]](team-notes.md)`, where `team-notes` is private. `LINK = \[([^\]]+)\]\([^)]*\)` does not match, so the raw `[notes [v2]](team-notes.md)` text, target included, lands in the record's `text` field. Probe1 output: `"text":"Proposed in chat. See [notes [v2]](team-notes.md). …"`. Only the private concept's ID/path leaks, not its content, and only when the author writes nested brackets. FR-3 and §4.7 ("Link targets never reach the index") still say it should not happen. - Fix: strip links with the same renderer-parser helper suggested above. Add a test with a nested-bracket link to a private concept. ### [security] Redaction runs on raw Markdown, so Markdown syntax can split a match the reader still sees — `scripts/publish.py:88` - Severity: ~ (SHOULD; behaviour confirmed, but it needs unusual source text) - Classification: specification defect. The PRD's FR-8 design ("Every rule applies to all published text before rendering") is followed as written. - The redaction rules match the source text before rendering. Probe 5 appended `Esc: /home\/alice and 10.0.0\.12 and **Alice** Example` to a public concept. `--check` exited 0 and the redaction count was 0. The page rendered `Esc: /home/alice and 10.0.0.12 and Alice Example`, which a reader sees as the home path, the IP and the private name. Backslash escapes are unlikely by accident, but a bold name is plausible. A later spec revision could also scan (and redact) the rendered plain text. ### [performance] Backlinks and published-directory sets are recomputed per page, which makes publish time quadratic — `scripts/publish_model.py:87`, `scripts/publish_render.py:43` - Severity: ~ (SHOULD; a CLI that runs once per publish, not server code) - For each page, `backlinks()` re-sorts `public_ids()` and runs `classify_link` over every link of every public concept. `make_resolver`/`kept_index_lines` also rebuild `public_dirs()` each time. Measured end to end on a synthetic bundle with 1,501 public concepts and 10 links each (Python 3.12, this machine): `real 0m29.9s`. Attributing that time to these functions is a static inference; I did not profile it. A bundle of a few hundred concepts takes a few seconds. To make it linear, compute a reverse-link map and `public_dirs` once per model, for example with `functools.cached_property` or a precomputed dict in `build_model`/`render_site`. ### [docs] The private-strings behaviour goes beyond the PRD wording - Commit a4de29d changed `private_strings` from `re.escape(s)` to whitespace-run matching (`\s+` between words). This is stricter, which suits redaction, and README/references document it. The template comment still says "matched literally and case-insensitively". That is acceptable, but it could mention the line-break tolerance. No action is required. ## Coverage ### Changed-file ledger (37 files, diff vs origin/main 92a21fe) | File | Status | | --- | --- | | .github/workflows/ci.yml | Reviewed: adds pytest install and a `python -m pytest -q tests` step after the selftest (matches WI-1). | | scripts/publish.py | Reviewed: flow, finding ordering, `--out` safety, marker rebuild, redaction copies, check-mode line math. | | scripts/publish_model.py | Reviewed: walk, visibility fail-closed, trust tier, classify_link rules 1-10, body_start_line, index frontmatter offsets. | | scripts/publish_redact.py | Reviewed: profile validation, rule order, literal replacement, scan never returns matched text. | | scripts/publish_markdown.py | Reviewed: escaping (all text runs and attributes escaped, `\x00` stripped before placeholder use), `safe_href`, fences, lists, tables, footnotes, autolinks. No XSS path found. | | scripts/publish_render.py | Reviewed: blocker in `kept_index_lines`; page shell, relative hrefs, generated listings, backlinks are otherwise correct. | | scripts/publish_search.py | Reviewed: advisory on `search_text`. | | scripts/publish_assets/search.js | Reviewed: uses only `textContent`/`setAttribute`/`createElement`; no `innerHTML`, `eval` or external URL; scoring matches §4.7. | | scripts/publish_assets/style.css | Grep-checked only: no `@import`, `url(` or `http`. It has a system font stack, `max-width: 48rem` and a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block. I did not read individual rules. | | scripts/selftest.sh | Reviewed: only the command loop gains `publish` (NFR-3). | | templates/okf-publish.yaml | Reviewed: id list matches DEFAULT_RULES; loads cleanly (covered by the test). | | README.md, SKILL.md, docs/USAGE.md, references/publish.md | Reviewed: command rows identical in both tables; sections present; the "never published … titles in index listings" claim is currently false (blocker). | | tests/conftest.py, tests/test_harness.py | Read in full. | | tests/test_publish_*.py (6) | Partly read. I checked that every function name the PRD lists is present, plus extras (75 tests pass in CI). I read the bodies of `test_no_unresolved_links`, `test_no_private_or_secret_bytes`, `test_out_safety` and `test_check_index_line_after_frontmatter_and_dropped_lines`; they assert what the PRD requires. For the other tests I rely on the CI pass. No test covers bracketed or unbalanced titles, filenames with spaces, multi-line descriptions or nested-bracket links. | | tests/fixtures/publish_bundle/** (11 files) | Read in full (except `rules/index.md`, read through the probe copy). They match the PRD fixture table. | | .pan/drafts/OKF-11.md, .pan/specs/…xbrief.json, .pan/continues/OKF-11.xbrief.json | Not applicable for code review: planning artifacts. I read the PRD for requirements. | NFR-3 check: `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` touches no existing script except `scripts/selftest.sh`; okf_common.py, validate.py, reindex.py and the template scripts are unchanged. ### Dimensions - Correctness: one blocker (index filtering), one advisory (search text). Visibility resolution, link classification, line numbers, `--out` safety and determinism are correct as traced. - Security: the renderer's HTML escaping and href scheme checks hold. The private-content leak is the blocker. The redaction pre-render gap is a hypothesis. - Performance: quadratic backlinks (advisory, measured). - Requirements/UX: see the matrix below. ### Acceptance criteria | AC | Status | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | AC-1 pytest in CI | Met | ci.yml step; CI log `75 passed in 2.58s` (run 43757998023). | | AC-2 Markdown renderer | Met | test_publish_markdown passes in CI; escaping traced manually. | | AC-3 redaction rules | Met | test_publish_redact passes; `scan` returns ids and lines only. | | AC-4 publish model | Met | test_publish_model passes. | | AC-5 site pages: "private listing lines are dropped" | **Unmet** for reindex-generated lines with bracketed titles or multi-line descriptions (blocker). Met for the fixture's simple lines. | | AC-6 search | Met for the unit tests (`search.js` has no `innerHTML`). Browser UAT is the test role's job, not verified here. Advisory on nested-bracket targets. | | AC-7 `--out` | Met per the CI tests. `test_no_private_or_secret_bytes` passes only because the fixture has no bracketed titles. | | AC-8 `--check` gate | Met (test passes in CI). | | AC-9 selftest | Met: CI log `ok - SKILL.md documents /okf publish`. | | AC-10 docs | Met: `## Publishing a bundle` at README:102. It contains `x_visibility`, `okf-publish.yaml`, `cloudflare/wrangler-action@v3` and `publish.py --bundle . --check`. references/publish.md lists all seven P_* codes. | ## Verification - `gh pr checks 12`: both `selftest` jobs pass on HEAD 2aa7417. The CI job runs `bash scripts/selftest.sh` and `python -m pytest -q tests` (75 passed). I reused this run and did not re-run the full suite. - Probe 1 (scratchpad probe1): hand-added bracketed private listing line plus nested-bracket body link. Private title and description appear in `out/rules/index.html`, and the private target appears in `search-index.json`. - Probe 4 (scratchpad probe4): the same leak using the real `reindex.py` output for a bracketed title and a multi-line description. `--check` exits 0 and `--out` publishes the private text. - Probe 5 (scratchpad probe5): a filename with a space and an unbalanced `]` title, both private, leak through reindex → publish. The escape and emphasis split defeats redaction and `--check`. - Probe 2: the `templates/repo` bundle passes `--check` (0 public concepts), so its README.md/CONTRIBUTING.md frontmatter causes no parse errors. - Probe 3: synthetic 1,501-concept bundle, publish took 29.9 s. - `npm run lint:effect-diagnostics`: not applicable (Python/stdlib repo with no TypeScript or Effect). - All probes ran in the session scratchpad. No tracked files were edited. ## Scope Note - The manifest's `acceptanceCriteria` list was empty. I used PRD §3 (FR/NFR) and §7 (AC-1 to AC-10) from `.pan/drafts/OKF-11.md` as the acceptance criteria. - The local `main` ref in this worktree does not match the PR base (`origin/main` 92a21fe). The PR diff itself is correct.
